title: Priority evidence capsule and rollback suggestion generator
creator: Evelyn Chen
description:
Background:
Redwood’s oncall flow currently floods PagerDuty/Slack with raw alerts and long trace dumps. Engineers spend the first 15-30 minutes manually collecting relevant traces, latency histograms, recent deploy markers, and a concise hypothesis. That slows MTTR and makes postmortem drafting inconsistent.

Goal:
Build an automated "evidence capsule" that attaches to PD/SMS/Slack alerts and includes a prioritized, deduplicated set of artifacts (top traces, error rate spike graphs, recent deploys, correlated logs, and relevant KV cache metrics). As part of the capsule, surface a rollback suggestion generator that proposes safe mitigation steps (e.g., rollback candidate, model variant fallback, or throttling knob) with confidence levels and links to the Console rollback action. The capsule should also seed a draft postmortem in Confluence/Drive when an incident passes severity threshold S2+.

Scope:
- Generate evidence capsule payloads for PagerDuty incidents and Slack incident threads.
- Capsule consists of: 1) prioritized trace snippets (summaries + links to full trace), 2) latency/error sparkline images, 3) recent deploy IDs with commit links, 4) top 3 log snippets correlated by trace ids, 5) candidate mitigations with rationale and confidence score.
- Provide an opt-in auto-seed postmortem draft (title, timeline start/end, hypothesis, implicated services, initial action items) in Drive when incident severity is high.
- UI: Add a "Capsule" button to Console incident view to regenerate and attach latest capsule.

Non-goals:
- Replacing human-run playbooks or fully automated remediation. The generator provides suggestions only; runbooks remain operator-driven.

Design overview:
1) Triggering: an incident hook from PD/alertmanager calls the "capsule service" with incident context (alert IDs, top spans, service tags). For Slack, a slash-command or message action can request generation.
2) Prioritization: capsule service scores signals from traces/logs/metrics by impact, user-facing latency impact, recent deploys and error budget burn. Uses heuristics + small ML ranking model (deferred to research phase) to order artifacts.
3) Rollback suggestion generator: lightweight rule engine + model-version mapping table to produce suggestions (rollback commit, switch to previous model variant, or toggle circuit-breakers). Each suggestion includes confidence and preconditions.
4) Postmortem seeding: draft saved to Drive with links; ticket metadata written back to PD Slack thread.

Data flow / integrations:
- Tracing: query jaeger/tempo for top spans using trace ids from alert payload.
- Metrics: query Cortex/Prometheus for 1h and 24h latency/error distributions and produce sparklines via Chart-renderer service.
- Logs: fetch correlated logs from Loki/Elasticsearch with trace ID filter.
- Deploys: query Deploy metadata service for recent releases in time window.
- Secret/permissions: capsule service reads deploy metadata and can create Drive drafts via service account (scoped).

API changes / contract:
- New endpoint: POST /api/v1/capsule/generate (auth: service token). Input: incident_id, alert_ids, primary_service, optional trace_ids. Output: JSON with summary, artifacts list (each artifact = string link), actions (list).
- PD integration: PD webhook subscription to append capsule as attachment using PD API v2.
- Slack: generate an ephemeral or thread message with condensed capsule and a "Open capsule in Console" button that uses console deep-link.

Acceptance criteria:
- Capsule generates within 10s for common small incidents (<= 3 traces) and within 45s for complex incidents (<= 20 traces).
- PagerDuty incidents show a capsule attachment with at least the top trace summary, latency sparkline, and the highest-confidence mitigation suggestion.
- Console incident page shows "Capsule" panel with links to full artifacts and an action to seed postmortem.
- Postmortem drafts are created for S2+ incidents and include incident metadata, timeline placeholders, and the capsule's hypothesis text.
- Unit and e2e tests cover trace fetching, ranking heuristics, and Drive/PD integration mock flows.

Rollout plan:
Phase 1 (canary): 2% of alerts routed to capsule service for internal Redwood teams only; manual verification required.
Phase 2: expand to 25% with automated QA checks on artifact completeness.
Phase 3: general availability for all customers with an opt-out toggle.

Metrics to track:
- Capsule generation latency (P50/P90/P99).
- Percent of incidents with at least one artifact link clicked within 15m.
- Time-to-first-action (operator acknowledgement / mitigation) comparing incidents with vs without capsule.
- False positive mitigation suggestions (operators marking suggestion as irrelevant).

Risks & mitigations:
- Sensitive data exposure in attachments: ensure redaction step for logs and persist only safe links; Drive drafts saved under restricted service account and audited.
- Overreliance on suggestions: UI emphasizes suggestions as non-authoritative; require explicit operator confirmation for automated rollback actions.
- Latency: pre-warm caches for common queries; fall back to a lightweight summary if full fetch times out.

Notes and follow-ups:
- We should coordinate with Security for Drive SA ACL review (see Security review ticket).
- Evaluate whether the lightweight ranking model is necessary in Phase 1 or can be heuristics-only.
- Need design microcopy for suggestions/confidence labels in Console.

2026-03-08 | Security (Liam O'Driscoll): Requested a short ADR for Drive SA scoping and retention policy. Flagging that logs must be redacted before seeding drafts.
2026-03-09 | Carlos Mendes: Implemented heuristics ranking (latency impact * error rate delta) and cut initial payload size. Benchmarked generation at ~8s for test incident fixture.
2026-03-10 | UX (Nadia Singh): Dropped in a mockup for Console capsule panel: added 'Regenerate' and 'Seed postmortem' CTA. Shared in #design-ops for feedback.
2026-03-11 | QA (Jorge Alvarez): Completed integration tests against mocked PD/Drive services. Found a bug where postmortem drafts used wrong timezone for timeline; fixed in PR #18.
